solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Gift of prophesy in age of superstition? (10)

blocks.note: the power of knowing what is coming
the era before rational enquiry, split into a prefix and a noun

annotation.surface: A seer's powers are traced back to a credulous era.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading: split the answer as PRE-SCIENCE and it names the time before science.
annotation.definitionFit: Prescience is foreknowledge, the very gift a prophet claims.

entries.clue: Watering holes where motherless cougar meets “discontented” bears (4)

indicators.note: MA (mother) is taken away
the contents are emptied out, leaving only the outer letters

annotation.surface: A big cat and some bears gather at a water hole in the wild.
annotation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around "discontented" signal it is to be taken literally: bears with their contents gone.
annotation.definitionFit: Watering holes is jokey slang for pubs, places people go to drink.

entries.clue: Feller boosted by mark in test (4)

indicators.note: in a down clue, pushing a word up turns it over

blocks.note: AXE, a tool that fells trees, turned upwards
M is the abbreviation for mark

annotation.surface: A man's score is lifted by a mark in a test.
annotation.walkthrough: "Feller" looks like a man; here it is literally a thing that fells, an axe.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an exam, short for examination, is a formal test of knowledge.

entries.clue: Kazakh journalist under arrest abandoning resistance or partner (12)

indicators.note: in a down clue, BORAT sits below COLLA
to abandon something is to leave it behind, so the arrest word leaves its R behind

blocks.note: COLLAR (arrest) without R, the symbol for resistance
Borat, Sacha Baron Cohen's spoof Kazakh reporter

annotation.surface: A Kazakh reporter, detained, is cut off from any resistance group or ally.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a news report of a detained journalist; "or" looks like a connective but is just two letters of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A collaborator is someone who works with you, a partner.

entries.clue: Build sports field in middle of hometown (5)

indicators.note: REC goes inside the other letters
only the central letters of hometown are used

blocks.note: a rec is a recreation ground
the central two letters of HOMETOWN

annotation.surface: A town builds a new playing field at its centre.
annotation.walkthrough: A rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public park with playing fields.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: putting up a structure, a tower or a tent, is both building it and erecting it.

entries.clue: Right-wing type and media boss were hanging out (9)

annotation.surface: A conservative figure and a press baron have been seen together.
annotation.walkthrough: "Right-wing type" reads as one person, but it splits: Con is short for Conservative, the British right-wing party, and type is a separate word.
annotation.definitionFit: To consort with people is to keep company with them, to hang out.

entries.clue: Witches wanting cold place to put Hansel and Gretel? (4)

annotation.definition: place to put Hansel and Gretel?

indicators.note: lacking, so the C is removed

blocks.note: a coven is a gathering of witches
C for cold, as on a tap; removed

annotation.surface: Witches, spurning the cold, want a warm spot for two captured children.
annotation.walkthrough: In the fairy tale the witch plans to cook Hansel and Gretel in her oven; the question mark marks the definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: The witch in the story tries to shove the children into her oven.

entries.clue: Big house in America sheltering character that’s rotund and evil (10)

indicators.note: the letters round O hold it inside

blocks.note: a villa is a large house

annotation.surface: An American mansion is home to a fat, wicked figure.
annotation.walkthrough: "Character" means a letter of the alphabet here, and the roundest one is O.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: behaving like a villain, the wicked character of a story, is being evil.

entries.clue: Blew money endlessly on loose ladies (10)

indicators.note: the last letter of MONEY goes
the letters are set free to rearrange

annotation.surface: Someone squandered cash on women of easy virtue.
annotation.walkthrough: "Loose ladies" is a ready-made phrase, but "loose" is the anagram signal and "ladies" alone is the definition: the answer is the opposite of the scene.
annotation.definitionFit: Lady is also a title held by women of the peerage, so aristocratic women are ladies, the opposite of the loose ones the surface suggests.

entries.clue: Times and equals on either side of sum, of course (2,3,5)

indicators.note: BY and MEANS sit at each end, with ALL between

blocks.note: as in six times four, six by four
one thing means, or equals, another

annotation.surface: An arithmetic lesson: multiplication and equals signs flank a sum.
annotation.walkthrough: The maths words all have everyday senses: multiplying is 'by', a sum is 'all', and 'equals' is 'means'.
annotation.definitionFit: By all means and of course are both ways of saying yes, certainly.

entries.clue: Flipping onion perhaps makes you cry (4)

indicators.note: turning the word over, back to front

blocks.note: an onion is an example of a bulb

annotation.surface: Chopping onions brings tears to your eyes.
annotation.walkthrough: "Flipping" looks like a mild British swear word or like chopping; it is the instruction to turn BULB round.
annotation.definitionFit: To blub is to cry, in informal British English.

entries.clue: Eccentric chaps abducted by alien being removed (12)

indicators.note: carried off inside, so the other letters go into ET

blocks.note: ET, the film alien; first half

annotation.surface: Some odd men are taken aboard a flying saucer and vanish.
annotation.walkthrough: ET, from the Spielberg film, is the crossword's standard alien. "Eccentric" looks like an anagram signal but just means STRANGE.
annotation.definitionFit: Estrangement is the state of being removed or distanced from others.

entries.clue: It’s useless to speak of something Orion’s belt might go round? (5,2,5)

annotation.definitionNote: WASTE OF SPACE is a noun phrase: 'it's useless' means 'it's a waste of space'

indicators.note: we are told what the answer sounds like when spoken

blocks.clueFragment: something Orion’s belt might go round
blocks.note: Orion's belt is a star pattern, so the waist it circles belongs to space

annotation.surface: Talking about a constellation's girth is pointless.
annotation.walkthrough: Orion is a hunter in the sky, and the three stars of his belt would sit round his waist: the WAIST of space.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: calling a person or thing a pointless occupier of room is a British put-down meaning it serves no purpose.

entries.clue: Explanation for inevitable failure of potato salad (7,3)

blocks.note: murphy is an old slang word for a potato

annotation.surface: Someone asks why a potato salad was always going to go wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of MURPHY'S takes no letter, so MURPHY and SLAW run together. Murphy's Law says whatever can go wrong will.
annotation.definitionFit: Murphy's Law, 'anything that can go wrong will', explains inevitable failure.

entries.clue: Power source conserving energy, like Natural History Museum? (6,4)

indicators.note: to conserve is to keep something safely held, so the other letters hold E within them

blocks.note: a made-up adjective on the pattern of 'plentiful': full of fossils, as the museum is
E is the symbol for energy

annotation.surface: An energy source that saves power is compared to a London museum.
annotation.walkthrough: The Natural History Museum in London is famous for its dinosaur fossils. The E goes between the U and the final L.
annotation.definitionFit: Coal, oil and gas are fossil fuels, sources of power.

entries.clue: A specialist in close encounters, I got fouls dubiously (9)

indicators.note: the letters are in a doubtful, unreliable order

annotation.surface: A footballer admits being penalised for rough tackles.
annotation.walkthrough: "Close encounters" sounds like physical contact on a pitch, which fits the fouls; it is the UFO phrase from Spielberg's film.
annotation.definitionFit: A ufologist studies reported UFO sightings, close encounters with aliens.

entries.clue: Sunak’s back to lead moderate Tories, turning up for meal (5,4)

indicators.note: the back letter of RISHI moves to the front
in a down clue, WETS is read upwards

blocks.note: RISHI, Sunak's first name, with its last letter brought to the front

annotation.surface: A political report: Rishi Sunak comes back to lead the Conservative moderates.
annotation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was a British prime minister. Wets was Margaret Thatcher's name for the moderate Tories who opposed her.
annotation.definitionFit: Irish stew, of lamb, potatoes and onions, is a meal.

entries.clue: Composition featuring rearrangement of Da Do Ron Ron’s middle parts (5)

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order
only the two middle words of the song title are used

blocks.clueFragment: Da Do Ron Ron’s middle parts
blocks.note: the middle words of the title, DO and RON

annotation.surface: A piece of music reworks a 1960s pop hit.
annotation.walkthrough: Da Doo Ron Ron was a 1963 hit for the Crystals; "middle parts" picks its second and third words.
annotation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical composition with a recurring theme.

entries.clue: A strand to slurp, as tagliatelle? (5)

annotation.definition: A strand to slurp, as tagliatelle?

blocks.note: the letters run across slurP AS TAgliatelle

annotation.surface: Someone describes eating a ribbon of tagliatelle.
annotation.walkthrough: There is no signal word: the answer is strung through "slurp, as tagliatelle", and the whole clue describes it.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: tagliatelle is a ribbon noodle, so the whole clue reads straight as a description of the food it hides.

entries.clue: Contract bridge beyond fashionable (9)

indicators.note: beyond means further on, so the bridge word is placed further along, after the fashionable one

blocks.note: a dental bridge is a partial denture

annotation.surface: Someone plays contract bridge, a game past its fashionable days.
annotation.walkthrough: "Contract bridge" is a card game, but the definition is "Contract" alone and "bridge" is dental.
annotation.definitionFit: An indenture is a legal contract, especially one binding an apprentice.

entries.clue: Scream more excitedly about 1980s band singer (12)

indicators.note: MORE is stirred up into a new order
the rearranged MORE goes round WHAM

annotation.surface: A fan screams louder for the vocalist of an eighties band.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface puts us at a pop concert, but the singer is a songbird: the yellowhammer is a common British bunting.
annotation.definitionFit: The yellowhammer is a songbird, and birds are singers in crosswords.

entries.clue: Massachusetts, one New England state nearby (5)

annotation.surface: A geography note: Massachusetts and a neighbouring New England state.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: Maine is a state near Massachusetts, both in New England.
annotation.definitionFit: Maine lies just north of Massachusetts, across a sliver of New Hampshire.

entries.clue: Name of four Holy Roman Emperors and eight from Italy (4)

annotation.definition: Name of four Holy Roman Emperors

blocks.clueFragment: Name of four Holy Roman Emperors
blocks.note: four medieval German emperors shared this name, numbered I to IV
the Italian word for the number 8

annotation.surface: A history quiz: a name shared by emperors and by eight Italians.
annotation.walkthrough: "Eight from Italy" looks like eight more people; it is the Italian word for the number.
annotation.definitionFit: A double definition: one sense is a historical first name, the other a foreign numeral, and the same four letters serve both.

entries.clue: Unfounded belief in enemy threat (4)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words

blocks.note: enemY THreat, with MY and TH joined

annotation.surface: Fear of an enemy attack turns out to be groundless.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is one complete idea, which hides that "in" is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A myth is a widely held but false belief.

entries.clue: Praise God for speakers of RP (4)

indicators.note: the answer is how the word sounds in the mouths of speakers of Received Pronunciation, who do not sound an R before a consonant

annotation.surface: A hymn line: praise God, in the accent of the BBC.
annotation.walkthrough: RP, Received Pronunciation, is the standard upper-class southern English accent; it does not sound the R in LORD.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, somewhat formal: to laud someone is to praise them highly, as in 'much-lauded'.

entries.clue: Cunning, with concealed weapon, making loud demands (10)

annotation.definitionNote: STRIDENTLY is an adverb; the definition describes the manner of demanding

indicators.note: SLY has TRIDENT hidden inside it

annotation.surface: An armed schemer shouts demands.
annotation.walkthrough: "Concealed" suggests a hidden word, but here SLY wraps around a whole weapon.
annotation.definitionFit: Strident describes a harsh, insistent voice or campaign, so demanding loudly is doing it in that manner.

entries.clue: Art going to fade? (4)

blocks.note: archaic second person: 'thou art going to' said with the old form of 'will'

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether art is destined to decline.
annotation.walkthrough: "Art" is not painting but the old verb: 'thou art' means 'you are', so 'art going to' is 'wilt', you will.
annotation.definitionFit: A flower that wilts fades and droops.

entries.clue: Chocoholic’s weakness also seen in the West’s degeneracy (5,5)

indicators.note: TOO joins the letters of THE WEST
the letters have fallen into disorder

annotation.surface: A chocolate addiction is blamed on Western decadence.
annotation.walkthrough: "Degeneracy" works as a noun signal: the fodder's letters degenerate out of order.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone with a sweet tooth loves sugary food; it is the chocoholic's weakness.
